sections.title: Lesson 5.1: Characteristics of Options
sections.overview: Options are derivative contracts deriving value from an underlying asset (stock, index, interest rate, or foreign currency). A two-party contract gives the buyer (long, holder) the right to exercise and obligates the seller (writer, short) to perform if assigned. The four basic positions—long call, short call, long put, short put—each have defined market attitudes, breakeven points, maximum gains, and maximum losses.
key_concepts: Derivative: contract whose value derives from an underlying asset; futures (commodities) are NOT securities, options ARE securities.
Buyer/holder/long: pays premium, owns the right to exercise, risks losing only the premium paid.
Seller/writer/short: receives premium, obligated to perform if assigned, profits if contract expires worthless.
Opening purchase → closing sale (long side); Opening sale → closing purchase (short side).
One equity option contract = 100 shares of underlying stock.
Call buyer = BULLISH (right to BUY at strike); Call writer = BEARISH (obligated to SELL at strike).
Put buyer = BEARISH (right to SELL at strike); Put writer = BULLISH (obligated to BUY at strike).
In-the-money (ITM): Call when stock > strike; Put when stock < strike.
At-the-money (ATM): stock = strike (for both calls and puts).
Out-of-the-money (OTM): Call when stock < strike; Put when stock > strike.
Intrinsic value: amount option is ITM; never negative (zero if ATM or OTM).
Premium = Intrinsic Value + Time Value (IV + TV = Pr).
Time value affected by: time to expiration and volatility (more of either = more TV).
Parity: premium equals intrinsic value.
Equity options: American-style exercise (any time before expiration); expire third Friday of expiration month at 11:59 pm ET.
Nonequity options: index options (broad-based like SPX/OEX, narrow-based, VIX), interest rate (yield-based), and currency options.
Index options: $100 multiplier, cash-settled, exercise settles next business day, broad-based stop trading 4:15 pm ET, narrow-based 4:00 pm ET.
Interest rate (yield-based) options: European-style exercise only; strike of 35 = 3.5% yield; each 1% = $1,000.
Currency options: European-style exercise only; exporters buy puts, importers buy calls; do NOT exist on U.S. dollar.
Hedging: protective put (long stock + long put); protective call (short stock + long call).
Covered call: writer owns underlying stock — conservative income strategy.
Uncovered (naked) call: unlimited risk (stock can rise infinitely).
Covered put: writer has cash or is short the underlying stock.
Naked put: max loss = strike − premium (substantial but not unlimited).
Spot Bitcoin ETPs approved by SEC 1/10/2024; spot Ether ETPs approved 5/23/2024 — part of registered-product universe.
rules: OCC (Options Clearing Corporation): issuer, guarantor, and clearing agent for all listed options; standardizes contract terms.
CBOE: principal options exchange and regulator.
Options Disclosure Document (ODD): must be delivered at or before account approval.
Account approval: must be approved by a Registered Options Principal (ROP) before any trading.
Trading may begin immediately after ROP approval; signed options agreement must be returned within 15 days of account approval.
If options agreement not returned within 15 days: only closing transactions allowed.
Premium settlement: T+1 (next business day).
Exercise of equity option delivering stock: settles T+1 (moved from T+2 to T+1 effective 5/28/2024).
Index option exercise settles next business day in cash.
Automatic exercise: any contract ITM by at least $0.01 at expiration exercised automatically unless 'do not exercise' instructions given.
Listed options trade 9:30 am–4:00 pm ET; expire third Friday at 11:59 pm ET.
OCC assigns exercise notices to short BDs randomly; BDs may assign to customers randomly, FIFO, or any fair method.
FINRA Rule 2360: Options.
formulas: Call Intrinsic Value = Stock Price − Strike Price (if positive, else 0)
Put Intrinsic Value = Strike Price − Stock Price (if positive, else 0)
Long Call: BE = Strike + Premium; MG = unlimited; ML = Premium
Short Call: BE = Strike + Premium; MG = Premium; ML = unlimited
Long Put: BE = Strike − Premium; MG = Strike − Premium (BE down to 0); ML = Premium
Short Put: BE = Strike − Premium; MG = Premium; ML = Strike − Premium
Protective Put BE = Stock Purchase Price + Premium
Protective Call BE = Short Sale Price − Premium
Index Option Total Premium = Quoted Premium × $100
Index Option Exercise Value = (Index Value − Strike) × $100 (for call)
Yield-based Option Payout = (Yield Difference in basis points / 100) × $100 per contract; each 1% = $1,000
mnemonics: CBOLA / PSBOSA: Call Buyer = Bullish, Owns right, Long, pays premium / Call Seller = Bearish, Obligation to Sell, Short, receives premium.
EPIC: Exporters buy Puts, Importers buy Calls (currency options).
Calls go UP, Puts go DOWN (direction owner wants stock to move).
'OCC starts with O for Obligation guarantor' — OCC issues and guarantees performance.
American = Anytime exercise; European = Expiration day only (yield-based and currency = European).

sections.title: Lesson 5.2: Municipal Fund Securities
sections.overview: Municipal fund securities are state/local government–sponsored investment products under MSRB jurisdiction. The three categories tested are Section 529 plans (education savings), Local Government Investment Pools (LGIPs), and ABLE accounts (for individuals with disabilities). Each is sold with an official statement (not a prospectus) and offers specific tax advantages.
key_concepts: Two types of 529 plans: (1) Prepaid Tuition Plans — lock in current tuition rates, state-resident plans, hedge against tuition inflation; (2) College Savings Plans — invest contributions for later use on qualified education expenses.
529 contributions: made with after-tax dollars, treated as gifts under federal tax law, no income limitations on donor.
529 earnings: grow tax-deferred; withdrawals tax-free at federal level if used for qualified education expenses.
Qualified expenses include K-12 tuition up to $10,000/year; no $10,000 limit on post-secondary qualified expenses.
Donor retains control of 529 account even after beneficiary reaches age of majority.
Beneficiary can be changed to a family member of the original beneficiary without penalty.
Scholarship exception: equivalent value may be withdrawn penalty-free (income tax on gains still applies).
Rollovers between state 529 plans permitted but no more than once every 12 months.
SECURE 2.0 (effective 2024): 529-to-Roth IRA rollovers permitted — $35,000 lifetime cap, account must be 15+ years old, annual rollover capped at IRA contribution limit.
Out-of-state 529 plans may forfeit state tax advantages (deductibility, tax-free withdrawals at state level).
LGIPs: established by states for OTHER GOVERNMENT ENTITIES (cities, counties, school districts) to invest short-term funds — NOT for retail investors.
LGIPs operate similarly to money market funds (often maintain stable $1 NAV) but are NOT money market funds.
LGIPs are NOT required to register with SEC (governmental exemption); no prospectus, but disclosure documents include information statement, investment policy, operating procedures.
ABLE accounts: tax-advantaged savings for individuals with significant disabilities (ABLE Act of 2014).
ABLE eligibility: onset of disability must have occurred before age 26 (beneficiary may currently be older).
ABLE: beneficiary is the account owner; income is tax-free.
ABLE: SSI/SSDI recipients meeting age criteria automatically qualify.
Only ONE ABLE account per person; annual contribution limit applies; contributions made with after-tax dollars.
rules: MSRB has jurisdiction over municipal fund securities (529s, LGIPs, ABLE).
MSRB Rule D-12: Definition of Municipal Fund Securities.
MSRB Rule G-45: Reporting of Information on Municipal Fund Securities.
MSRB Rule G-17: Conduct of municipal securities activities (fair dealing).
Sale of 529 plan must be accompanied or preceded by an official statement / offering circular.
529 nonqualified withdrawals: gains subject to ordinary income tax PLUS 10% penalty.
mnemonics: Prepaid = Price locked; Savings = Stock-market-like growth.
ABLE 26: disability must onset Before age 26.
LGIPs = Local Government Investment Pools (Local Governments are the investors, not individuals).

sections.title: Lesson 5.3: Partnerships
sections.overview: Partnerships are unincorporated associations of two or more individuals. General partnerships are not securities, but limited partnerships (LPs) — often called direct participation programs (DPPs) — are securities that pass income, losses, and tax benefits directly through to investors. Hedge funds are commonly organized as LPs and sold via private placement.
key_concepts: General Partnership: all partners are general partners (GPs), share management responsibility, unlimited personal liability, results flow through to partners for tax purposes.
Partnership is a tax-REPORTING entity but NOT a tax-PAYING entity.
Limited Partnership (LP) requires at least one GP and one Limited Partner.
GP: unlimited liability, manages partnership, fiduciary duty to investors, cannot compete, cannot borrow from partnership, cannot commingle funds.

Limited Partner: limited liability (only invested capital at risk), no management role (loses limited liability if participates in day-to-day management), votes on overall objectives, receives distributions, may inspect books, may sue GP.
LPs are highly illiquid — virtually no secondary market; transfers require GP approval.
LPs sold publicly = prospectus; sold privately (private placement) = private placement memorandum (PPM); private placements typically require accredited investors.
Property in LPs often held as Tenants in Common (TIC).
Dissolution priority: (1) Secured lenders, (2) Other creditors, (3) Limited partners (profits first, then capital), (4) General partners.
Tax deductions that reduce taxable income without reducing cash flow: depreciation, depletion, accelerated depreciation, intangible drilling costs (IDCs).
Passive income/losses: income from LPs is passive; passive losses can offset passive income only — NOT ordinary income.
Recapture of tax benefit: if IRS disallows prior deduction, limited partners owe back taxes, penalties, and interest.
Hedge funds: typically organized as LPs, sold as private placements, not subject to mutual fund rules.
Hedge fund strategies: high leverage, short selling, derivatives, currency/commodity speculation, emerging markets.
Hedge funds have lockup provisions (minimum holding periods), high minimum investments, limited number of investors.
rules: FINRA Rule 2310: Direct Participation Programs.
Limited partner who participates in management may lose limited-liability status.
LP must complete a partnership agreement; if amended, amended agreement must be obtained annually if changes occur.
Passive losses deductible only against passive income (NOT the $3,000/year capital loss rule).
formulas: Cash Flow = Net Income (Loss) + Depreciation (and other non-cash deductions)
Investor's share of partnership income/loss = Ownership % × Partnership Income/Loss
mnemonics: Dissolution order — 'Secured Other Limited General' (SOLG): Secured creditors → Other creditors → Limited partners → General partners.
GP = Greater liability; LP = Limited liability.
DPP benefits: 'DAID' — Depreciation, Accelerated depreciation, Intangible drilling costs, Depletion.

sections.title: Lesson 5.4: REITs, ETFs, and ETNs
sections.overview: REITs pool investor capital to invest in real estate equity, mortgages, or both, passing through income (but not losses) under the conduit theory. ETFs are exchange-traded baskets of securities (typically index-tracking) that trade intraday like stocks. ETNs are unsecured debt obligations of an issuer whose return is linked to an index — exposing investors to issuer credit risk.
key_concepts: REIT types by holdings: Equity REIT (owns property), Mortgage REIT (owns mortgages on property), Hybrid REIT (both).
REIT types by registration/listing: Public listed (exchange traded), Public non-listed (registered with SEC but not exchange-listed), Private (not registered).
Non-listed REITs: difficult to price, less liquid, greater risk.
REITs are NOT investment companies and NOT DPPs — losses do NOT pass through.
REIT taxation (conduit/pipeline theory): avoids corporate tax if 75%+ of income from real estate AND 90%+ of net investment income distributed to shareholders (Subchapter M).
Investors hold an undivided interest in a pool of real estate investments.
ETFs: typically track an index, registered as open-end funds or UITs, trade intraday on exchanges like stocks.
ETF advantages vs. mutual funds: intraday pricing, marginable, can be sold short, lower operating expenses, greater tax efficiency.
ETF disadvantages vs. mutual funds: commissions on each trade, temptation to overtrade, market-driven price may diverge from NAV.
ETF pricing: subject to supply/demand forces; may trade above or below NAV.
ETNs: unsecured debt securities issued by banks/financial institutions — backed only by issuer's credit.
ETNs: have stated maturity, pay NO interest, offer NO principal protection; investor receives cash payment linked to index performance minus fees at maturity.
ETN primary risks: DEFAULT/CREDIT risk (issuer), market risk (index linked), liquidity risk (few are actually exchange-listed).
ETNs may trade at a premium to inherent value due to limited issue size — premium buyers may suffer losses at maturity.
Spot Bitcoin ETPs approved by SEC 1/10/2024 (Rel. 34-99306); spot Ether ETPs approved 5/23/2024.
rules: Subchapter M (IRC): REIT must distribute 90%+ of net investment income and receive 75%+ of income from real estate to qualify for conduit tax treatment.
REITs are subject to SEC registration if public; private REITs are exempt.
ETFs registered under Investment Company Act of 1940 as open-end funds or UITs.
ETNs are debt securities — not registered investment companies.
formulas: REIT qualification: ≥75% income from real estate AND ≥90% net investment income distributed
ETN Maturity Payment = Principal × (Index Performance) − Management Fees
mnemonics: REIT = '75/90' for Subchapter M conduit treatment.
REITs pass through INCOME, not LOSSES (DPPs pass through both).
ETF = Equity-like Trading Fund (trades like stock); ETN = Exchange-Traded Note (debt, default risk).
Three REIT registration types: Private, Public Non-listed, Public Listed (P-PN-PL).
